I will still plant mainly the way I know works here. I have done this for many years, and I do not like changing too much in one season. Cotton is still my main crop, because on my land with well water it is steady, and if I keep fertilizer and water on time, I can still get a decent harvest. I will use improved seed for cotton, not the old saved kind, because now most people around me use better seed and it comes up more even. I will put most of my land into cotton and keep a smaller piece for stevia. Stevia needs more careful cutting and drying, so I will not spread it too wide since some people in my family work outside and labor is not always enough.

For fertilizer, I will not cut too hard. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more. I usually start from what I did before and then look at the stand and rain. On cotton I will give a heavier base, then topdress later when it starts growing fast and setting bolls. On stevia I will keep nitrogen a bit lower than cotton, but I will not let potash be short because I want stronger growth and better leaves. Since I have well irrigation, I will water when the seedlings need help, again before fast growth, and again in the key period. For pests, I will spray when I see pressure rising, especially aphids, bollworm, and leaf problems on cotton. I do not like wasting money on too many sprays, but I also do not wait until the field is badly hit. I will plough before planting because my land size is not tiny anymore, and I want the soil loosened and the fertilizer mixed in well.
